svg.text: Three schedule() calls: chunking, decode and one preemption
Token budget 16 · max_num_seqs 4 · block_size 4 · 8 free KV blocks · chunked prefill on · FCFS
A: prompt 10, max_tokens 4 B: prompt 12, max_tokens 4 C: prompt 6, max_tokens 4 (all wait at step 1)
Step 1: A fits whole, B gets the rest of the budget
Running pass: empty. Waiting pass: A takes 10 tokens, B takes a 6-token chunk. C waits: budget 0.
RUNNING computed 6/12 -> chunk, no token 2 blocks
WAITING budget used up: the pass stops
Step 2: A decodes, B ends its prompt, C starts
Running pass: A 1 token, B its last 6 prompt tokens. Waiting pass: C fits (2 blocks), 13 of 16 used.
RUNNING 6 tokens -> prompt done, token 1 3 blocks
Step 3: B needs a 4th block, none is free: preempt C
B has 13 tokens = 4 blocks. allocate_slots returns None, so the last running request (C) is preempted.
PREEMPTED blocks freed, computed 0, front of waiting
No waiting pass in this step (a request was preempted). C later recomputes 7 tokens (6 prompt + 1 output).
Simplified: synchronous steps (the default AsyncScheduler plans step k+1 before the token of step k arrives), no EOS,
block 0 (the null block) not drawn. In step 3 the pool frees C's blocks in reverse order: block 8 (not full) goes to the
front of the free queue and B gets it; block 7 (full, cached) goes to the end. C can hit it later, unless a request pops it first.
